name: FTEQW
summary: A QuakeWorld-derived engine that also plays NetQuake, with the widest server feature set of the six.
description:
FTEQW publishes rolling autobuilds rather than numbered releases, which is what `engine_version` says. Its server settings are QuakeWorld's, so the host actions here set `maxclients` through `+set` rather than using NetQuake's `maxplayers` console command — the one place these six engines' documented command lines genuinely differ.

This profile was written from FTEQW's own published command-line documentation, not from a build running on this machine. That is what every `unverified` platform below means, and it is why there is no version probe: asking a Quake engine what version it is means starting it, and starting it means opening a window and a game.

`play_map` names a game directory as well as a map, because that is what these engines' command lines do: `-game` chooses which directory the map is loaded from. Launching a map into a directory nobody named is how you end up watching the wrong map.

Game data — PAK files, maps, textures and sounds shipped with a commercial release — is not covered by that licence, and the Companion never copies, uploads or redistributes it.
